text.p: Mercury Finance Co said Wednesday that it discovered some accounting irregularities which caused an overstatement of some previously released earnings.

According to John Brincat, president and chief executive officer, the irregularities appear to be the result of unauthorized entries being made to the accounting records of the company by the principal accounting officer.
Based on the findings and analysis to date, it appears that the previously reported net income for fiscal years 1993 to 1996 will be restated.

As a result of overstatement of earnings, the company said it is in violation of certain covenants in its debt agreements. The company said it is in discussion with its lenders regarding its borrowing arrangements.
Mercury Finance said it believes that its financial condition remains strong and will support the company's continuing operations and plans for future growth.
The principal accounting officer was last in Mercury's office the night of January 23, the day the company released its fourth-quarter earnings, a Mercury spokesman said.
"He called Friday and said he would not be in for personal reasons," the spokesman said. "They haven't seen him since."

As a result of the adjustments, shareholders' equity as of December 31, 1996, would be reduced from $353 million to $263 million. The estimated restated amounts are the subject of ongoing analyses. The company said it expects that its independent public accountants will complete the audit for the 1996 fiscal year by March 31, 1997.

The spokesman said Mercury is still optimistic that it will be able to move forward with its planned acquisition of BankBoston Corp's Fidelity Acceptance Corp, a deal that was valued on January 10 at $392.5 million.
BankBoston said Wednesday it would evaluate the results of an investigation into Mercury's accounting before proceeding with the deal.
Mercury Finance said net income for fiscal years 1993-1996 will be restated as follows:
1993 previously reported net of $64.9 million or $0.37 a share will be restated to $64.2 million and $0.37.
1994 previously reported net of $86.5 million or $0.49 a share will be restated to $83 million and $0.47.
1995 previously reported net of $98.9 million or $0.57 a share will be restated to $76.9 million or $0.44.
1996 previously reported net of $120.7 million or $0.70 a share will be restated to $56.7 million or $0.33.
Trading in shares of Mercury has been halted.
